caps.text: SafeNight. Go out together. Get home together.
A consent-based safety app for friends on a night out.
Nights out have a gap nobody owns.
Friends split up. The designated driver has a drink.
A location pin says where someone is, not that anyone is coming.
Built for groups of friends, designated drivers, and safety buddies.
Roles are accepted on purpose, never assigned silently.
Plan. Stay connected. Notice a concern. Coordinate help. Confirm home.
A temporary group that expires. Not a tracker, not a dispatcher.
Sharing is opt-in, scoped per person, time-limited, revocable.
No intoxication detection. Nobody is ever declared sober.
People confirm every outcome. The agent never acts alone.
Explicit driver acceptance. Instant deterministic warnings.
And an agent that adapts when a buddy does not answer.
Live demo. Four phones, four identities, one SpacetimeDB database.
Each phone registered its identity. Alex sets up the demo group.
The roster: Alex organizes, Sam explicitly accepted the driver role.
Each person grants each friend specific scopes, for a limited time.
The map shows only consented, approximate locations. Simulated tonight.
Alex reports a concern: Sam, the driver, may have been drinking.
Sam sees "Do not drive" instantly. A deterministic rule, no AI in the loop.
The incident opened the agent. Plan v1 comes from Nemotron on NVIDIA NIM.
Every tool call is validated, then recorded as a receipt. Messages are SIMULATED.
Maya, the primary buddy, gets the request. She does not respond.
The follow-up timer lives in SpacetimeDB. We advance it instead of waiting two minutes.
No reply. The agent escalates: Nemotron plan v2 messages Jordan, the backup.
Jordan acknowledges. Sent is not acknowledged: the states stay distinct.
Now the agent looks up transport and proposes a ride. Two tool rounds.
Routing was unreachable, so it says "Provider link only". Nothing is invented.
Sam picks a ride. The app opens a link; a person books. No autonomous purchases.
Booked by a person. The agent tells Jordan and waits for pickup.
Pickup confirmed. Only Sam can close this: the agent never resolves an incident.
Home, confirmed by the person. The incident resolves for everyone.
Under the hood: SpacetimeDB is the whole backend. No API server.
Sessions, consent, incidents, timers, agent state: all tables and reducers.
An event table with row-level security delivers the warning only to Sam.
Safety rules run first, in one transaction, before any model is called.
Consent-scoped views. "I'm okay" never closes an incident. Humans resolve.
The agent is a scheduled procedure calling Nemotron 3.5 Super with a tool allowlist.
Tool results are fed back for up to three rounds. Every call is validated first.
Receipts say who proposed each step: the model, a policy rule, or a simulation.
This is the real plan from tonight's run, with the model name and receipts.
81 module tests and 93 web tests, plus a live four-identity end-to-end run.
Revocation, unauthorized access, duplicates, escalation, injection: all covered.
Nemotron and SpacetimeDB are live. SMS is simulated until Twilio keys exist.
Adding keys changes nothing in the data model, only who writes the plan.
SafeNight. NVIDIA Nemotron agentic workflow on a SpacetimeDB backend.
